section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Delaware is known as the 'First State' partly because it was first to ratify the U.S. Constitution. Delaware also had one of the nation's first comprehensive seat belt laws. Which occupants must wear a seatbelt in Delaware today?
options: a:Only the driver,b:Driver and front-seat passengers only,c:All occupants in the vehicle,d:Only passengers under age 18
note: Delaware requires all vehicle occupants — front and rear — to wear a seatbelt. Delaware has primary enforcement, meaning officers can stop a vehicle solely for a seatbelt violation. Delaware's early adoption of comprehensive seatbelt laws reflects its historical role as a legislative pioneer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a learner's permit in Delaware?
options: a:14,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Delaware requires applicants to be at least 16 years old to apply for a learner's permit. This is older than many states that allow permits at 15 or 15½. After holding the permit for 6 months and meeting supervised driving requirements, they can apply for a Level 2 license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for adult drivers (age 21+) in Delaware?
note: Delaware's per se DUI limit is 0.08% BAC for adult drivers. Commercial drivers face a 0.04% limit. A BAC of 0.08% or higher is sufficient for a DUI charge regardless of apparent impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Delaware's zero tolerance law, the illegal BAC for drivers under 21 is:
note: Delaware sets the underage DUI threshold at 0.02% BAC. A driver under 21 with a BAC at or above 0.02% faces license revocation and criminal penalties. This effectively makes any alcohol consumption illegal before driving for underage drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Delaware's GDL program, how many hours of supervised driving must a Level 1 permit holder complete before applying for a Level 2 license?
options: a:20 hours including 5 at night,b:30 hours including 10 at night,c:40 hours including 10 at night,d:50 hours including 10 at night
note: Delaware requires 50 hours of supervised driving practice, including at least 10 hours at night, before a Level 1 permit holder can apply for a Level 2 restricted license. This practice must be certified by a parent or legal guardian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on most urban streets in Delaware when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Delaware's default speed limit in urban areas is 25 mph where no limit is posted. Always check for posted signs — many streets have limits that differ from the default, and school zones have even lower limits when active.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, what does the GDL nighttime restriction require for Level 2 (restricted) license holders under 18?
options: a:No nighttime restriction applies,b:No driving between 10 PM and 6 AM,c:No driving between midnight and 5 AM,d:No driving after 9 PM
note: Delaware Level 2 restricted license holders under 18 may not drive between 10 PM and 6 AM unless accompanied by a licensed adult 25 or older in the front seat, or driving to/from work or school with documentation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when a school bus stops on a two-lane Delaware road and activates its flashing red lights?
options: a:Stop only if driving behind the bus,b:Slow to 15 mph and proceed,c:Stop in both directions at least 20 feet from the bus until lights stop flashing,d:Yield only when children are visible crossing
note: Delaware law requires vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm. You may not proceed until the lights stop flashing and the arm retracts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in a Delaware school zone when children are present?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph,d:25 mph
note: Delaware school zones have a 20 mph speed limit when children are present or warning lights are active. Slow down well before entering the zone and remain alert for children on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Delaware highway and see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights. What does the Move Over law require?
options: a:Slow to 25 mph and maintain your lane,b:Move one lane away from the stopped vehicle if safe; if not, slow to a safe speed,c:Stop completely until the vehicle moves,d:Only move over for police — not tow trucks or utility vehicles
note: Delaware's Move Over law requires drivers to vacate the lane adjacent to any stopped emergency, law enforcement, towing, or highway maintenance vehicle with flashing lights. If a lane change is not safe, slow to a speed that is reasonable for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Delaware interstates?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Delaware's maximum interstate speed limit is 65 mph. Delaware is a small, densely populated state where traffic is heavy near Wilmington and Dover. Urban sections of interstates are often posted at lower limits — always follow posted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, what does a flashing yellow light mean at an intersection?
options: a:Stop completely and yield before proceeding,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:The signal is broken — treat it as a 4-way stop,d:Do not enter the intersection under any circumstances
note: A flashing yellow light is a caution indicator in Delaware. Reduce speed and proceed carefully — a full stop is not required (unlike a flashing red, which requires a complete stop). Scan carefully for crossing vehicles and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane Delaware road, a solid yellow line is on your side of the center. You want to pass the vehicle ahead. You may:
options: a:Pass if you can do so in under 5 seconds,b:Pass only if the other car is going more than 10 mph under the limit,c:Not pass — the solid yellow on your side prohibits crossing the center line,d:Pass only if you first signal for 100 feet
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the road is an absolute prohibition on crossing the center line to pass. Wait for a dashed yellow line on your side before attempting to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Delaware's implied consent law, refusing a chemical test after a DUI stop results in:
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a constitutional right,b:A 1-year license revocation for first refusal,c:Only a fine with no license action,d:A warning only on the first offense
note: Delaware's implied consent law means driving on public roads constitutes consent to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal results in a 1-year license revocation separate from any DUI charge. Refusal can also be introduced as evidence against you in court.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended in Delaware for normal driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Delaware recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. In rain, fog, or heavy traffic — common near Delaware's urban corridors — increase to 4–6 seconds. More space equals more reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you turn right on a red light in Delaware?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if no pedestrians are visible,d:Only on non-school days between 7 AM and 9 PM
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Delaware after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic. Always check for 'No Turn on Red' signs before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver in Delaware is approaching a yield sign. What is required?
options: a:Stop completely regardless of traffic,b:Slow down and yield to traffic; stop only if necessary,c:Maintain speed and merge when safe,d:Flash headlights to signal your presence
note: A yield sign requires you to slow down and give the right of way to cross traffic or pedestrians. Stop if necessary to avoid a collision, but a full stop is not required when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are stopped at a Delaware intersection on a red light. The light turns green, but a large truck is still in the intersection. You should:
options: a:Honk to alert the truck and proceed — you have a green,b:Wait for the intersection to clear completely before entering,c:Flash your headlights and move forward,d:Change lanes to go around the truck
note: A green light gives you the right of way but does not guarantee the intersection is clear. Delaware's defensive driving principle requires you to ensure the path is fully clear — especially for large vehicles that take longer to clear — before entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action when you see a pedestrian with a visual impairment (white cane or guide dog) at a crosswalk in Delaware?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph and pass carefully,b:Stop completely and yield the roadway until the pedestrian has crossed safely,c:Honk to alert the pedestrian you are there,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is in your direct lane
note: Delaware law requires drivers to stop and yield completely to any pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog. These individuals are visually impaired and may not see your vehicle. Do not proceed until the pedestrian has completely and safely crossed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the shape and color of a warning sign in Delaware indicate?
options: a:Red octagon — stop required,b:Yellow diamond — potential hazard ahead,c:White rectangle — regulatory rule,d:Orange rectangle — construction zone
note: Yellow diamond-shaped signs are warning signs in Delaware and across the United States. They alert drivers to potential hazards ahead — curves, school zones, pedestrian crossings, merges, and more — and require extra alertness and often a reduction in speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from behind, you must:
options: a:Accelerate to the next intersection and pull off,b:Stop immediately in your current lane,c:Pull to the right side of the road and stop until it passes,d:Move to the left lane and reduce speed
note: Delaware law requires drivers to pull to the right side of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from any direction. Remain stopped until the vehicle has fully passed before resuming travel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most Delaware rural roads and highways when no sign is posted?
options: a:45 mph,b:50 mph,c:55 mph,d:60 mph
note: Delaware's default speed limit on rural roads and highways without a posted limit is 55 mph. Always check for signs — many rural routes have posted limits that may differ from the 55 mph default.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in Delaware and see a flashing red traffic signal. What must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic, then proceed when safe — same as a stop sign,c:Treat it as a green light since no cross traffic is using the intersection,d:Stop only if another vehicle is approaching from the cross street
note: A flashing red signal must be treated as a stop sign in Delaware. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians in all directions, and proceed when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking on a street in Delaware, your wheels must be within how many inches of the curb?
options: a:6 inches,b:12 inches,c:18 inches,d:24 inches
note: Delaware law requires parallel-parked vehicles to be within 12 inches of the curb. Parking too far from the curb creates a hazard for passing vehicles and cyclists, and is a citable parking violation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, how many feet before a turn must you begin signaling?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet,d:300 feet
note: Delaware requires drivers to signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Signaling early gives surrounding drivers and pedestrians adequate time to respond. Failing to signal is a moving violation in Delaware.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You see a person in a marked crosswalk in Delaware. What must you do?
options: a:Slow to 15 mph and proceed if the person is in a different lane,b:Stop and remain stopped until the person has completely crossed the road,c:Honk once and proceed if the way is clear,d:Yield only if they have already begun crossing
note: Delaware law requires drivers to stop and yield the entire roadway to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You may not proceed until the pedestrian has completely crossed — even if they are in a different lane. Pedestrian right-of-way is absolute in a marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, what is the consequence of a first-offense DUI for an adult driver?
options: a:Warning letter and fine only,b:License revocation, fines, possible jail time, and mandatory alcohol treatment,c:Fine only — no license action on a first offense,d:Community service only
note: A first DUI conviction in Delaware results in license revocation, fines, possible jail time, and mandatory participation in an alcohol treatment program. Delaware's DUI penalties are designed to deter repeat offenses.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a Delaware multi-lane road, you see a sign that reads 'Keep Right Except to Pass.' This means:
options: a:You must always stay in the right lane regardless of speed,b:The left lane is reserved for passing only — use the right lane for normal travel,c:Right lane is for trucks only,d:The sign only applies to drivers below the speed limit
note: Delaware's 'Keep Right Except to Pass' rule requires drivers to use the right lane for normal travel on multi-lane roads and use the left lane only for passing. After passing, return to the right lane. This rule reduces tailgating and road rage on highways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a railroad crossing in Delaware with flashing red lights and lowering gates. What must you do?
options: a:Stop before the gates fully lower and proceed before a train arrives,b:Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until the gates fully rise,c:Slow down to 10 mph and proceed quickly before the train arrives,d:Stop only if you can actually see a train approaching
note: When railroad crossing lights flash and gates begin lowering, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until the gates fully rise before proceeding. Never try to beat a train — trains cannot stop quickly and impacts are almost always fatal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal definition of reckless driving in Delaware?
options: a:Any speed exceeding the posted limit by 10 mph or more,b:Operating a vehicle with willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property,c:Any use of a cell phone while driving,d:Driving through a school zone above 25 mph
note: Reckless driving in Delaware is defined as operating a vehicle with willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property. It is a criminal offense — not just a traffic ticket — and can result in license suspension, fines, and possible imprisonment.

section-name: Special Situations & Road Users
question: What is true about large trucks compared to passenger vehicles?
options: a:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow very quick stops.,c:They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances than passenger vehicles; a truck at 55 mph may need almost twice the distance.

section-name: Vehicle Ownership & Responsibilities
question: Why should you use antifreeze washer fluid in cold climates?
options: a:Cold fluid can scratch your windshield.,b:It will keep the washer fluid from freezing.,c:Moisture can cause cold wiper blades to crack.
note: Antifreeze washer fluid prevents freezing so you can clear salt, dirt, and slush from the windshield in winter.

section-name: Alcohol, Drugs & Impaired Driving
question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Vision.,b:Judgment.,c:Balance.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, then affects coordination and vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should begin your turn from:
options: a:The lane closest to the centerline.,b:The right-hand side of the road.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, begin in the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the nearest legal lane.

section-name: Alcohol, Drugs & Impaired Driving
question: What happens as your BAC increases?
options: a:You become more sober.,b:You become more intoxicated.,c:You become more coordinated.
note: As blood alcohol concentration rises, a person's level of intoxication and impairment increases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you not start across an intersection because you might block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Unless you entered on a green light.,b:Under any circumstances you should avoid entering if you cannot clear it before the light turns red.,c:Unless you entered on a yellow light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it before the light turns red; blocking an intersection can lead to a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: Do not change lanes within an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Using your high beams in fog.,b:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Staring fixedly at the road ahead.
note: To stay aware of hazards, scan the road and check mirrors every 2–5 seconds. Do not use high beams in fog; use low beams instead.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: If your car starts to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.
note: In a skid, do not brake; steer gently in the desired direction until control returns.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: When driving at night, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Always use your high beams.
note: At night, increase your following distance when visibility is reduced and avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights to prevent glare.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: Before entering an intersection, what scanning sequence should you use?
options: a:Look only to the right.,b:Look left,c:Look only to the left.
note: Look left, right, then left again before entering an intersection because vehicles from the left will be closer.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: When is a wet highway surface most likely to be especially slippery?
options: a:If it has been raining for one to two hours.,b:If it has been raining several hours.,c:If it has just begun to rain.
note: Road surfaces are often most slippery when rain first starts because oil and dirt on the pavement mix with the rain to form a slick film.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,b:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it has passed.,c:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.

section-name: Signs, Signals & Road Markings
question: A curb painted red indicates:
options: a:A loading zone.,b:An area reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking
note: A red-painted curb means you may not stop, stand, or park in that area.

section-name: Vehicle Ownership & Responsibilities
question: Why should you keep the inside of your windows clean if someone has been smoking?
options: a:Dust tends to settle on the insides of car windows.,b:Smoking causes a film to build up on the glass inside the vehicle.,c:The stale smell can be distracting.
note: Smoke deposits produce a film on glass that reduces visibility; keep windows clean for safety.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake lightly to slow, then pull off safely.,b:Apply the brake and hold it down hard.,c:Pull over immediately without slowing gradually.
note: If a tire blows, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, brake lightly, and steer to a safe place off the roadway.

section-name: Signs, Signals & Road Markings
question: What do "No passing zone" signs indicate?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:To maintain a steady speed.,c:That it is not safe to pass.
note: A "No passing zone" sign indicates that passing is not permitted and would be unsafe in that area.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes and wait to drift to a stop.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: For vehicles with ABS, press the brake firmly and the system will pump the brakes automatically.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: To be able to turn quickly, your hands should be placed:
options: a:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,b:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Both hands should be on opposite sides of the steering wheel to promote comfortable, controlled turns, especially at higher speeds.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: In traffic moving 50–55 mph, you are least likely to be involved in a crash if you:
options: a:Stay within that speed range.,b:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.,c:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
note: Matching the flow of traffic (while obeying speed limits) minimizes speed differentials between vehicles, reducing the chance of collisions.
